A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CUB benchmark. Their main text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching relocated content.

before.justification: v2 reports original CMT evaluations across CounterFact, NQ, and DRUID, including BCU, accuracy, CCU, and feature-correlation results.

after.justification: v3 retains these original evaluations and adds GPT-4.1 model results, a Qwen–Llama comparison, Pareto analysis, and case studies.

M1.justification: The seven CMT procedures, fine-tuning approach, PH3 intervention mechanism, and multi-agent Algorithm 1 remain unchanged. Additional model evaluations and the revised COIECD hyperparameter do not introduce a new algorithmic component.

E1.justification: Evaluation retains CounterFact sentence completion, NQ question answering, and DRUID fact checking under gold, conflicting, and irrelevant contexts. The four fine-tuning datasets also remain unchanged. Added models and context-length descriptions do not introduce new task or scenario coverage.

E2.justification: v3 adds Regular GPT-4.1 and GPT-4.1 mini reference models alongside their Prompting and Multi-agent evaluations. Appendix B also introduces an evaluated Regular Llama 3.1-8B comparator against Qwen 7B in Figures 5–6. The original seven CMT comparison methods remain.

E3.justification: v3 extends evaluation to additional model configurations and introduces a Pareto comparison using aggregated faithfulness and robustness scores. COIECD's reported lambda for Qwen 7B-Instruct changes from 0.50 to 0.25 (v2 Table 16; v3 Table 26), without establishing that experiments were rerun. Existing splits, primary metrics, and fine-tuning settings remain.

E4.justification: v3 adds a substantial analytical layer: faithfulness–robustness Pareto analysis in Section 6.3, nine context-specific case tables examining predictions and probabilities in Appendix A.5, and a Qwen–Llama model-selection comparison. Appendix C.4 additionally characterises context-length distributions. These extend v2's correlation, relevance-assessment, and data-quality analyses.

E5.justification: New Figures 5–6 show error bars for individual Qwen and Llama BCU scores, but their statistical meaning and calculation are unspecified. Existing cross-model standard deviations in Figure 3 and correlation significance annotations remain. No additional runs or seed counts are established.

E6.justification: v3 adds GPT-4.1 model score blocks, relevance and memorisation results, Llama results, and case-study and Pareto findings. Newly included GPT-4.1 achieves the highest Regular NQ BCU, 63.5 versus the retained Qwen 32B-Instruct score of 61.7. Input correlations also change: gold-NQ context length moves from -0.23 to -0.20 and distractor rate from -0.19 to -0.15. Retained BCU and accuracy entries and Figure 4's CCU values are unchanged.

T1.justification: Section 6.3 newly defines aggregate faithfulness as the average of gold and conflicting BCU, pairs it with irrelevant-context BCU as robustness, and specifies the nondominance criterion for Pareto selection. The original BCU and CCU definitions, including Equation 1, remain unchanged; no proofs are added.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims remain a comprehensive CMT benchmark, trade-offs between faithfulness and robustness, and inflated performance on synthetic compared with realistic datasets. Updating the study from nine models and approximately 750 experimental points to 11 models and approximately 800 points expands supporting evidence without redefining those contributions or conclusions.

C2.justification: Section 6.1 replaces the general suggestion that artificial contexts confuse larger models with a hypothesis linking sparse CounterFact evidence to stronger parametric beliefs. v3 also adds application-specific Pareto guidance and explanations for excluding reasoning models and using synthetic temporal conflicts. Existing language, long-context, and multi-document limitations remain.

D1.justification: v3 replaces the promised code release with a repository link and availability statement, supplies dated API model identifiers, and adds GPT prompt selections and approximately USD 110 in API costs. It revises the COIECD lambda entry and classifies Prompting inference cost as Low instead of Mid. Table 24 still describes repository release as future, leaving actual availability internally inconsistent.

R1.justification: v3 adds citations to Sun et al. (2025), Islam et al. (2026), and Mujahid et al. (2025), and expands positioning around standard-length versus long-context research. Numerous other bibliography changes update retained works to publication versions rather than introduce different cited research.

P1.justification: There are targeted rewrites of the abstract, model-selection rationale, CounterFact explanation, and limitations, plus author-note edits and new analytical subsections. Appendix numbering and some placement change, but the main narrative order and most existing method and implementation prose remain.

P2.justification: v3 adds the Pareto table, nine case-study tables, two Qwen–Llama figures, and a context-length figure. It expands model-result displays, adds context-length columns to dataset examples, and moves the input-correlation table into the main text. Existing plots are widened; Figure 4 redisplays unchanged CCU values.

improvement.justification: v3 broadens the empirical evidence and improves implementation documentation while retaining v2's core results. However, its new Pareto table has unexplained scope: Table 3 lists Qwen 7B-Instruct/Multi-agent at faithfulness 59.14 and robustness 73.32, although Table 6 gives GPT-4.1/Multi-agent approximately 63.85 and 76.0, exceeding both. New Table 10 also reports context-conditioned probabilities of 1.00 and 0.99 for different tokens in one Multi-agent row without explanation. These reporting problems make the net benefit of the added analyses uncertain.
